title: When the Weather Sings
premise: Xanthe Fairweather has spent eleven years writing postcards to their late brother's burned-down house, cataloguing in careful, unsent confessions everything they never told him—including the truth about the fire. When a radio station plays an unrecorded song only the two of them ever knew, Xanthe realizes someone else survived that night and has been carrying the same secret. Tracking the stranger down forces Xanthe to choose between protecting the family inheritance built on silence and telling a dying witness the truth that could free them both; they confess, forfeit the estate, and finally mail one last postcard to an address that no longer burns.
about_author: Ada Galloway is the pen name of a former rural postmistress who spent two decades reading other people's unsent letters before writing her own. She lives near the coast, where she keeps a drawer of postcards addressed to no one.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. We meet them mid-ritual: buying postcards, writing confessions to a dead brother at an address that burned years ago, filing each one in a shoebox of things never sent. A radio plays a song that was never recorded—one Xanthe and their brother wrote together the night he died. The beat is dread disguised as routine: someone else knows.

chapters.title: Stranger in the Old Photographs
chapters.summary: Xanthe traces the broadcast to a hospice volunteer named Marisol, who found a cassette among a dying man's effects—a man photographed beside Xanthe's brother on the last night. Rising tension: Marisol believes the song is a gift meant for her patient, while Xanthe recognizes it as evidence of what really started the fire. The emotional beat is loyalty pulling against truth as Xanthe lies to keep the past buried.

chapters.title: What the Fire Kept
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating between Xanthe and the dying stranger, Elias. At his bedside, Xanthe learns Elias was the brother's lover, blamed for the blaze, and that the brothers quarreled over the Fairweather inheritance the night it burned—with Xanthe's own silence sealing Elias's guilt. Confronted by Marisol with the photograph, Xanthe must speak the confession eleven years of postcards rehearsed. The beat is rupture: truth spoken too late to save, but not too late to matter.

chapters.title: Postage Due
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, weeks later. They sign away their claim to the estate, fund Elias's funeral, and give Marisol the song's true authorship. In the final scene, Xanthe writes one last postcard—addressed this time to themselves—and actually mails it, breaking the ritual of the unsent. The resolution lands on quiet justice outside any courtroom: forgiveness given, inheritance relinquished, invisibility ended.
